title: Judge the call, not the luck
principle: Judge a call by what you knew then, not the result.

screens.text: 2007 T20 World Cup final. Pakistan need 13 off the last over. Dhoni gives the ball to Joginder Sharma, who has played seven matches.

screens.prompt: Misbah had hit Harbhajan for three sixes in his last over. Was Joginder a good call?

options.label: No, it was a wild gamble

screens.why: After a wide, a miss and a six, Misbah tried a scoop. It went straight to Sreesanth, and India won by five runs. The call became famous.

screens.title: Resulting
screens.text: Annie Duke, a poker player, calls it 'resulting': judging a call by how it turned out. Good calls can lose. Bad ones can win.

screens.prompt: Same over, but the scoop clears fine leg for four. Pakistan win. Dhoni's call was…
screens.why: He knew the same things before the ball. Only the luck changed. The papers would have said 'blunder', and they'd have been resulting.

wrong.a: What did Dhoni know before the ball? Nothing changed but where the ball went.

screens.title: Four boxes
screens.text: Four boxes: good or bad call, with good or bad luck. After a big decision, ask which box you're in. Fix the call, not luck.

screens.prompt: A ₹50,000 fair stall wins Neha's coaching centre a ₹4 lakh school deal 1 time in 4. Average gain per fair?
screens.why: ¼ × ₹4,00,000 = ₹1,00,000 on average. Take off the ₹50,000 stall: ₹50,000 gained per fair, on average. It's a good bet.

wrong.a: That's what a winning fair brings. She wins only 1 in 4.
wrong.b: That's a losing fair. On average, the wins pay for the misses and more.

screens.prompt: At 1 win in 4, how often will Neha leave with nothing two fairs in a row?
screens.why: She misses 3 times in 4. Two misses in a row: ¾ × ¾ = 9/16, about 56 in 100, so it happens more often than not. A good bet can look bad for months.

wrong.a: That's two wins in a row: ¼ × ¼. Misses are the common case.
wrong.c: Missing once is ¾. Twice in a row is ¾ × ¾ = 9/16.

screens.prompt: Dev hired a cashier without checking anything. Sales then had their best month ever. What should Dev do next time?

options.label: Keep this cashier, but check the next hire
Hire the same quick way. It worked

screens.why: Nothing Dev knew made it a good call. The good month might be Diwali, or luck. A good result doesn't make a careless method good.

wrong.b: That's resulting. The sales say nothing about how he hired. Next time, check references.

screens.prompt: Mohan picked a new supplier. Which did he know then, and which only later?

items.text: On time for 3 other shops for years
Its truck broke down on the highway
Price ₹2 a kilo below the others
A strike shut its factory for a week

screens.why: Judge Mohan on the left side only. The breakdown and the strike are luck. He can plan for them, but they don't make the choice wrong.

screens.prompt: Put the steps of a fair decision review in order.
steps: Write down what you knew then
Write what you chose, and why
Ask: was it the thinking, or luck?
Change your method only if the thinking was wrong
screens.why: Look at the result last, so it can't colour how you judge the thinking.

screens.setup: Ravi's tempo service checked three references on a new client. Months later the client went bust, owing him ₹60,000. His partner says: 'No more new clients. Ever.'
screens.question: What do you do?

options.label: Agree. Old clients only from now
options.outcome: Ravi is safe for a year. Then two old clients move away, and he has no new ones to replace them.
options.why: One bad result made him drop a sound method.
options.better: Keep checking new clients, and cap how much each can owe.

options.label: Keep the checks, and cap what new clients owe
options.outcome: Ravi keeps winning new clients. No new client can owe more than ₹20,000, so the next bad one hurts a third as much.
options.why: The checks were sound; the loss was partly luck. He kept the method and fixed what he could learn from.

options.label: Ignore it. Bad luck happens
options.outcome: Ravi carries on as before. The next bust client could owe him just as much.
options.why: Right that it was mostly luck, but he learned nothing he could use.
options.better: Ask what he could control next time, like how much one client can owe.

summary: Judge a decision by what you knew when you made it.
A good bet can lose many times in a row. Don't drop it after one miss.
Learn from the thinking, not from the luck.

cards.front: You checked everything, and the deal still failed. Was it a bad decision?
options: Not if the thinking was sound
cards.back: Judge what you knew then. A good call can have a bad result.

cards.front: A bet wins 1 time in 4. How often do you lose twice in a row?
cards.back: ¾ × ¾ = 9/16. Losing streaks are normal on good bets.

sources.label: The greatest T20 finals: India vs Pakistan, 2007 (The Cricket Monthly)
